xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5084: Telemetry: CI runs, test homes and throwaway VMs report as new installs (5,818 of 5,824 ids are one-day ghosts)

plan.title: Telemetry: CI runs, test homes and throwaway VMs report as new installs (5,818 of 5,824 ids are one-day ghosts)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: About 30 files across 10 path prefixes, but most items are one-line env additions at harness spawn sites plus their tests and docs. The gate change (CI and temp-home exclusion), the env wiring and the install_kind tag fix one data-quality defect together: shipping the gate without the wiring leaves the <repo>/.tmp smoke homes and WSL leg minting ids, and shipping either without install_kind leaves the post-deploy PostHog filter with nothing to filter on. Each item is still independently reviewable and the DAG lets them run in parallel.

narratives.Problem: PostHog shows 5,824 distinct install ids in 30 days and only 6 were active on two or more days. Every fresh OVERDECK_HOME mints a new install id, and telemetry is off only under Vitest, NODE_ENV=test or OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0. ci.yml and windows-smoke.yml never set OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0, so every CI job that boots the server or runs the CLI, every agent test stack with an isolated home and every throwaway Fly VM reports as a new install, and the dashboards cannot show real adoption.
narratives.Proposal: Add automatic exclusions (CI env set; Overdeck home inside os.tmpdir(), /tmp or ~/.overdeck/tmp) to the one effective-state door resolveTelemetryEnabled() via a new resolveTelemetryState() with a fixed six-row precedence (env off > config off > OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=1 > CI > temp home > on), so Node, the Settings API and the browser all follow it. Set OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0 in ci.yml, windows-smoke.yml, the WSL probe script and every test harness that spawns a server or CLI. Stamp a closed-enum install_kind (user, remote_vm, dev_checkout, container) on every Node event and exception and as a browser super property; Fly provisioning writes a remote_vm marker file. Settings names the forced-off reason. Document everything in docs/TELEMETRY.md and configuration/telemetry.mdx.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Configuring the PostHog project internal-user filter or the usage dashboards (post-deploy Flywheel step)
- Deduplicating, deleting or backfilling historical ghost ids in PostHog
- Any change to install-id minting, the telemetry-id file name or its repair lock
- Tagging src/lib/remote/ work-agent VMs (they do not run pan telemetry paths)
- Detecting FLY_*, Kubernetes or container= env vars for install kind
- Browser-side CI detection (the browser follows effectiveEnabled)
- Phone app telemetry (PAN-5021)
- Changing telemetryBlockedForProcess() in service.ts
- Adding install_kind to TELEMETRY_EVENT_CATALOG or changing any event's typed properties
- Letting OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=1 override telemetry.enabled: false or OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0
- Raising any file-size allowlist cap

autoDecisions.summary: OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=1 cancels both automatic exclusions (CI and temporary home) but never overrides telemetry.enabled: false or OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0.
autoDecisions.rationale: An explicit user opt-out must not be beaten by a flag that exists for fixtures; fatal-process.test.ts spawns a tmpdir-home child with OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=1 under CI=true and expects capture, so =1 must beat both exclusions.

autoDecisions.summary: The exclusions live in resolveTelemetryEnabled()/resolveTelemetryState() in config.ts, not in telemetryBlockedForProcess() in service.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: The Settings API effectiveEnabled and the browser's initTelemetry only see resolveTelemetryEnabled; a service.ts gate would leave the browser SDK sending from CI dashboards.

autoDecisions.summary: CI/temp-home detection is a separate pure module src/lib/telemetry/environment.ts with injected inputs.
autoDecisions.rationale: The Vitest setup sets OVERDECK_HOME to a temp dir and GitHub sets CI=true, so suites that run the real resolver need a mockable seam; the detector gets direct tests.

autoDecisions.summary: Treat /tmp as a temporary root on POSIX in addition to os.tmpdir() and ~/.overdeck/tmp.
autoDecisions.rationale: Agent shells set TMPDIR to ~/.overdeck/tmp/..., so os.tmpdir() is not /tmp there, yet agents have created literal /tmp test homes.

autoDecisions.summary: remote_vm comes only from an Overdeck-written marker file ${OVERDECK_HOME}/install-kind; no FLY_* env sniffing; the marker accepts any of the four values.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue scopes remote_vm to Overdeck-provisioned machines; a user self-hosting on Fly is a real user. Accepting any domain value costs no extra code.

autoDecisions.summary: dev_checkout reuses the existing isDevMode() (src/ next to packageRoot), so the operator's pan reload generation dashboards report dev_checkout.
autoDecisions.rationale: One existing source-checkout test; the operator's own machines are exactly what the PostHog internal filter should drop.

autoDecisions.summary: container = /.dockerenv or /run/.containerenv only; precedence remote_vm > dev_checkout > container > user.
autoDecisions.rationale: Simplest reliable Docker/Podman signal; the more specific kinds win (a devcontainer source checkout is dev_checkout).

autoDecisions.summary: install_kind is a centrally stamped property and a TELEMETRY_PROPERTY_DOMAINS entry, not a TELEMETRY_EVENT_CATALOG property.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches platform/arch/clientType; adding it to the catalog would change all 25 event types and call sites.

autoDecisions.summary: Add disabledBy to the Settings API and show the real reason in the Settings status line.
autoDecisions.rationale: Without it, a CI or temp-home dashboard would claim 'Disabled by OVERDECK_TELEMETRY', and the footer's 'can only force telemetry off' becomes false.
windows-smoke.yml sets no WSLENV, so neither workflow env nor CI reaches the wsl-bash shell.

autoDecisions.summary: The scripts/anywhere/*-smoke.mjs scripts get explicit OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0 (kept in scope rather than moved to NonGoals).
autoDecisions.rationale: Their homes are <repo>/.tmp/..., outside every temp root, and the issue explicitly asks for OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0 where test harnesses spawn the server or CLI.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep one issue and set plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of splitting into sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: The surface is wide but shallow (one-line env additions plus tests and docs) and the halves only fix the data together.

items.title: Add the install_kind domain to the telemetry contract

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. In packages/contracts/src/telemetry.ts export `TELEMETRY_INSTALL_KINDS = ["user","remote_vm","dev_checkout","container"] as const`, add `install_kind: TELEMETRY_INSTALL_KINDS` to TELEMETRY_PROPERTY_DOMAINS (after `harness`), and export `type TelemetryInstallKind = TelemetryPropertyValue<"install_kind">`. Do NOT add install_kind to TELEMETRY_EVENT_CATALOG. In the same commit add the domain-table row `| \`install_kind\` | \`user\`, \`remote_vm\`, \`dev_checkout\`, \`container\` |` to docs/TELEMETRY.md after the `harness` row (the drift test parses that table). Add a schema test asserting the exact four values. Run `npm run build:contracts:incremental` so root tsc sees the new export.

items.title: Given the contract, when telemetry-schema.test.ts runs, then TELEMETRY_PROPERTY_DOMAINS.install_kind equals ['user','remote_vm','dev_checkout','container'] and the test passes

Create the install-kind resolver module

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. New src/lib/telemetry/install-kind.ts exporting INSTALL_KIND_FILENAME = 'install-kind', interface InstallKindProbe { overdeckHome; exists; readFile; isDevCheckout }, resolveInstallKind(probe = defaultProbe()) and a per-process cached getInstallKind(). Order: marker file `${overdeckHome}/install-kind` trimmed content when it is one of TELEMETRY_INSTALL_KINDS -> 'dev_checkout' when isDevMode() (src/lib/paths.ts) -> 'container' when /.dockerenv or /run/.containerenv exists -> 'user'. Every probe call is wrapped in try/catch so the function never throws. Tests use injected probes only (no real fs).

items.title: Given a marker containing 'remote_vm\n' and isDevCheckout true, when resolveInstallKind runs, then it returns 'remote_vm'

Given no marker, not a dev checkout, and exists('/.dockerenv') or exists('/run/.containerenv') true, then it returns 'container'; with neither it returns 'user'
Given readFile and exists probes that throw EACCES, when resolveInstallKind runs, then it returns a value and does not throw

In provisionFlyMachine step 5, directly after `await run(`chmod 600 ${shellQuote(identityPath)}`, 'Protecting the identity file');`, add `await deps.writeRemoteFile(machineName, `${overdeckHome}/${INSTALL_KIND_FILENAME}`, 'remote_vm\n');` with a PAN-5084 comment. Create the pure CI and temporary-home exclusion detector

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5. New src/lib/telemetry/environment.ts exporting type TelemetryAutoExclusion = 'ci' | 'temporary_home', interface TelemetryEnvironmentInputs { env; overdeckHome; temporaryRoots; realpath }, telemetryEnvironmentForcesOn(env = process.env) (true for trimmed lowercase '1' or 'true') and detectTelemetryAutoExclusion(inputs = defaultInputs()). CI counts when env.CI trimmed is non-empty and lowercase not '0'/'false'; CI is checked first. Temporary home: containment via path.relative: inside = !isAbsolute(rel) && rel !== '..' && !rel.startsWith('..' + sep) (rel '' is inside; never rel.startsWith('..'), which misses children named like '..smoke-123') over {resolve, realpath} of both home and each root, realpath failures fall back to the resolved form. defaultInputs: env process.env, overdeckHome getOverdeckHome(), temporaryRoots [os.tmpdir(), join(getCanonicalOverdeckHome(), 'tmp'), plus '/tmp' when not win32], realpath realpathSync. All tests inject inputs.

items.title: Given env CI 'true' or '1', when detectTelemetryAutoExclusion runs, then it returns 'ci'; given CI '0', 'false' or '' and a non-temp home it returns null
Given home '/tmp/odk-a-1', '/tmp/..smoke-123' or a home equal to a root, then it returns 'temporary_home'; given home '/tmpfoo/x' with root '/tmp' it returns null

Given home '/var/folders/ab/T/x', root '/var/folders/ab/T' and a realpath mapping both to '/private/var/...', then it returns 'temporary_home'; given realpath throwing, it still decides from the resolved paths
Given OVERDECK_TELEMETRY '1', 'true' or ' TRUE ', telemetryEnvironmentForcesOn returns true; given '0', 'yes' or unset it returns false
Add resolveTelemetryState with the six-row precedence table

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6. Rewrite src/lib/telemetry/config.ts: keep telemetryEnvironmentForcesOff(); add type TelemetryDisabledReason = 'environment' | 'config' | 'ci' | 'temporary_home', interface TelemetryState { enabled; disabledBy? }, and resolveTelemetryState(configuredEnabled?: boolean) applying, first match wins: OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0/false -> off 'environment' (checked before the config read; read YAML lazily as `configuredEnabled ?? loadConfigSync().config.telemetry?.enabled !== false` AFTER this row, never in a default parameter); config false -> off 'config'; telemetryEnvironmentForcesOn() -> on; detectTelemetryAutoExclusion() 'ci'/'temporary_home' -> off with that reason; else on. resolveTelemetryEnabled() returns resolveTelemetryState().enabled. In config.test.ts mock '../../../../src/lib/telemetry/environment.js' (spread the actual module, detectTelemetryAutoExclusion: vi.fn(() => null)) so the existing tests keep meaning under the temp-home Vitest setup and CI=true, then add one test per precedence row.

items.title: Given detectTelemetryAutoExclusion returns 'ci' and OVERDECK_TELEMETRY unset, when resolveTelemetryState runs, then it returns { enabled: false, disabledBy: 'ci' }; with 'temporary_home' it returns disabledBy 'temporary_home'
Given exclusion 'ci' and OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=1, then it returns { enabled: true }; given config enabled false and OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=1, then it returns { enabled: false, disabledBy: 'config' }

Given OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0 and exclusion 'ci', or OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=0 with loadConfigSync throwing, then resolveTelemetryState returns disabledBy 'environment'; given resolveTelemetryState(false), it returns disabledBy 'config' without consulting the YAML
Given fatal-process.test.ts spawns a child with a tmpdir home and OVERDECK_TELEMETRY=1, when it runs, then the child still posts the sanitized exception and the test passes
Return disabledBy and installKind from the Settings API through one door

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7. ApiTelemetryConfig gains optional disabledBy (TelemetryDisabledReason) and installKind (TelemetryInstallKind); validateApiTelemetryConfig accepts both when they are strings in their domains (the UI posts them back on save). telemetrySettingsFromConfig uses resolveTelemetryState() for effectiveEnabled + disabledBy (omitted when enabled) and getInstallKind() for installKind. Add mergeApiTelemetrySettings(current, updates) to settings-api-telemetry.ts building the save-response block (enabled from updates ?? current ?? true; effectiveEnabled/disabledBy from resolveTelemetryState(enabled); installId and installKind from current; operatorGrouping from updates ?? current ?? false; operatorHash from current). In settings-api.ts replace the 7-line inline telemetry block at ~1155-1161 (anchor `effectiveEnabled: !telemetryEnvironmentForcesOff()`) with `telemetry: mergeApiTelemetrySettings(current.telemetry, updates.telemetry),`, add the helper to the line-35 import and delete the line-43 telemetryEnvironmentForcesOff import. In settings-telemetry.test.ts mock environment.js (detect -> null by default) and install-kind.js (getInstallKind -> 'user'), update the two full-object toEqual expectations, and add the ci/temporary_home/validation cases.
